A client holds a connection slot forever without finishing the handshake (every Initial refreshes idle; open_timeout has no handshake deadline): one deadline set at accept, never refreshed, with a proved close; write the failing test first (check that on_frames accepts a PING-only Initial); RCA, class and catch; correct the shell's "55.6 min" comment. Owner decision 2026-11-10: Phase 6 (order 5) before 10a (order 6), so the deadline is proved once on the re-proved open_timeout.
MAX_CONNS (102) admission and slot eviction that assume RFC 9000 §10.1's 3·PTO floor (a slot held up to 55.6 min, 196 s for a dead peer with defaults).
Retry or a per-source handshake limit (each unauthenticated Initial costs a P-256 signature, ~15 ms, or RSA, 6 ms at 2048 and 45 ms at 4096 bits), or a faster proved exponentiation.

A random-keyed SipHash index for CIDs and reset tokens replaces route's linear scan (up to 512 CID and 816 constant-time token comparisons per datagram, sized for about 100 connections); a sorted Vec is not acceptable (leaks token order, RFC 9000 §10.3.1).

Path slots (MAX_PATHS 4) never evict: an on-path attacker forwarding a victim's packets from spoofed addresses fills them and the client's next NAT rebinding is dropped. Eviction conflicts with wf_amp for paths with logged sends.

An RSA key loader that establishes every rsa_key_wf clause (primality through a verified certificate check, d zero-padded to k octets) before an RSA certificate is accepted; until then a bad key panics or exhausts memory at the first ClientHello that selects it.

Every datagram makes the shell walk all connections (on_wake each loop turn, the target serviced twice): call on_wake only when deadline() <= now; check pipeline::settled_later's ordering assumptions; add a shell test.

Memory per connection may be ~6.4 MiB (REQ_BUF_CAP 65552 x 100 bidi streams), not the ~1 MiB of crates/server/src/lib.rs:100: trace whether reading re-issues credit past the windows, then fix the comment or the limits; a proved per-connection and server memory bound.
Transmit-loop termination is unproved (crates/quic/src/pipeline.rs:316-318); the shell caps polls per wake and, if the cap is ever hit, logs and spins at 1 kHz. Prove termination.

C10 unauthenticated resource exhaustion: ensures that unauthenticated-reachable tables grow only on a gated packet (Paths, CidTable, route, the shell's address table) and a generated handshake-CPU figure in TRUSTED. Was "scheduled 9r2", which never took it.
C15 ratio tests: for each streaming op in quic and h3, allocations and copied bytes at n, 2n, 4n scale at most linearly.
C18 unverified shell: a tracked seeded fuzz of Server::on_datagram/on_wake asserting slot growth only on gated packets and a settled deadline(); a getsockopt test for V6ONLY/DF.
The field-section encoder copies the section twice (performance only).

Test crypto_ooo_cost_linear (tests/crypto_cost.rs) checks linear allocations and time with no realloc. Not claimed: in-order delivery. take_front copying a whole run into CryptoStream's buf when a 1-byte frame closes a gap is O(r), which the per-call rule O(d + log n) (owner decision 2026-11-12) does not accept: cat-C15-9b2.

text: C3 residuals the carryover gate leaves: (1) a row added and deleted within any branch is never seen (on a branch only the merge-base copy is compared, on main only first-parent commits, so the merge is the one commit; fix: walk every commit of merge-base..HEAD); (2) closing evidence is checked to exist, not to close the item, and `doc:<path>` can close an unrelated row; (3) a merged cell accepts any ancestor commit, not the phase's merge; (4) a phase merged by a commit whose subject does not start `Merge phase-` is not tied to its status, and `Merge branch 'phase-X'` on a branch's first parent false-fails; (5) a TRUSTED `never (...)` cell is not ratcheted; (6) the untracked-evidence scan reads RCA Evidence lines, TRUSTED.md, requirements.md and crates/ only, not this tsv or the roadmap. frees (dropping chunks and nodes) and allocator calls (CapVec::new) are not in the ghost cost at all (9b2 T6 names them at quictls feed, receive's replaced stash and pump_backlog's refed stash; the parts `Streams::gc` drops, a "Data Read" ring's slot vector and the sending part, are charged per removal since 9b2 Task 10d (`c_gc()`, returned to the frame path, the ACK path and `deliver_some`; a loss removes nothing); a closing connection's `Streams` drop is charged since 9b2 Task 10b: moved whole to `Connection::dead` and freed a step per `backlog_step`, each entry's ring `c_rfree()` and queue `c_sfree()`, with the CRYPTO stores and the Initial and Handshake send contexts moved to their slots at Closed (`QuicServer::retire_closed`) and the shell removing a connection only once Closed and `!has_backlog()`; `deliver_some`'s removal charges `c_rfree() + c_sfree()`; still uncharged here: the Connection's own drop at removal: its packet records (the 1-RTT space's in flight), paths, CID and ACK tables and empty fixed buffers, no stream, store or tree); a literal cost returned by a match arm of avl::bal, frags::walk or frags::walk_run is not seen (the gate's keyed literal-return exemption, 9b2 T6 fix round 2); calls are matched by name, so streams.rs and recv_stream.rs (whose fns share names with cost fns) are callee-only (9b2 Task 10d fix round 1: their cost fns are callees of conn.rs, pipeline.rs and server.rs, so a drop at that boundary fails the gate, but their own bodies are unchecked: a call between their fns that drops a cost passes the gate and Verus alike, since the cost ensures bound amounts and cannot catch a drop, and only 9b2-M38, feed_stream's `deliver` charge, witnesses one there), and three calls that only share a cost fn's name are keyed exemptions (the gate's NOT_COSTS: pipeline.rs's `Connection::accept` and `Vec::clear`, conn.rs's `RecvPns::on_packet`; each fails if its target ever returns a cost): resolving callees by path/type (9b4 Task 4's VIR reader) ends both. Either MIR-step bounds for Frags::insert, after_insert and take_front by the verified ctmir cost analysis (the 9t4 machinery: tools/ct-driver/cost-targets.txt, theorem_cost_mir), or a ghost-cost discipline Verus itself enforces.

source: 9b2 Task 8 (2026-11-16); .superpowers/sdd/2026-11-13-phase-9b2-byte-queue/task-8-report.md; 9b2 Task 8 fix round 0 (2026-11-17); ruling 2026-11-17 (fix round 1)
text: CRYPTO send contexts on ByteQueue: `SendStream::write` requires `buffered + d <= MAX_QUEUE` (2^28, D10); `Streams::write` discharges it from `MAX_SEND_BUFFER`, but `Connection::crypto_write` (conn.rs) has no bound on the bytes TLS writes per level (quictls `on_send` passes each TLS `Send` event as it comes; nothing proves a per-level total), so it drops a write that would pass `MAX_QUEUE`, as a write past `VARINT_MAX` is already dropped (`let _ =`). Unreachable in practice (one server flight per level, a few KB plus the configured chain) but not proved. Close by proving a per-level bound on TLS output (tls `theorem_event_discipline` plus a configured-chain cap) and turning the guard into a requires; owner to be ruled by the controller (proposed 9b5, whose tls tasks own the TLS output path). Fix round 0 (ruling: no silent drop; prove from existing bounds or name the missing one): the guard stays, unproved; the per-Send bounds exist (tls flight.rs: ServerHello <= 0x1000, EncryptedExtensions <= 0x1000, Certificate <= 0x100_0004 under `cert_chain_ok`, CertificateVerify <= 0x1_0008, plus Finished; server.rs:1118 HelloRetryRequest <= 0x100), so one Send is far below 2^28. Missing, all three needed: (i) tls: no exported fact bounds the Send bytes per level over a connection: `theorem_event_discipline` gives only `spec_rank(s2) <= spec_rank(s)` and no data lengths, and `spec_call_shape` (which shows a call with a Send moves Start -> HrrSent or to WaitFinished) is private; needed: a call whose events hold a Send at level l strictly lowers the rank, with that call's Send bytes at l at most C_l (Initial: HRR + SH; Handshake: EE + Certificate + CV + Finished). (ii) quictls: no `QuicServer` invariant ties the bytes written to the CRYPTO send contexts to the TLS phase (a potential: written(l) + C_l(remaining in phase) <= MAX_QUEUE). (iii) quic: no spec accessor for `ctx_i`/`ctx_h` written bytes, and `crypto_kept` frames only the receive side (`crx_*`), so adding it means a clause in `crypto_kept_bg`, proved by every conn fn that ensures it, among them send_path_datagram (7.54M). Likely owner: 9b5 (D14, the TLS step and quictls `feed`), with (iii) a conn.rs task that splits the near-cap fns first; the controller to rule. Also: the same per-level bound would bound the CRYPTO contexts' queue capacity, which nothing counts today (review Minor 5). Ruling (2026-11-17): the guard stays for now; re-owned to 9b5, whose Stage C changes tls build_flight, the tls events and quictls, where the per-level Send-bytes bound (i), the quictls phase invariant (ii) and the conn crypto_kept spec (iii) belong; 9b5 must prove the guard unreachable and delete it. `spec_call_shape`'s shapes (Initial at most HRR + SH, Handshake one flight) make the guard dead in practice (Task 8 review).

text: SendStream on ByteQueue (D10) keeps its capacity until the queue is empty: `drop_front` frees nothing, and the queue requests at most `2 * max(MIN_CAP, 3*P)`, P the peak since it was last empty (the spec's Memory table accepts this per queue). Measured: 64 KiB written with the FIN, every 1 KiB piece but the last acknowledged: 310,272 bytes of capacity held for 1,024 buffered (before Task 8, split_off left about the tail). `Streams::send_room` counts lengths (`tx_buffered`), so a peer that withholds one ACK per stream frees send room while each part keeps up to about 6x its peak: per connection the requested bytes are bounded by the live sending parts times 6 MiB, not by `MAX_SEND_BUFFER`. Needs a ruling: accept (state the per-connection bound), or count requested bytes in `send_room`, or shrink a queue whose length falls below a fraction of its capacity (a de-amortized migration down). Closed (owner decisions 2026-11-16, count capacity, and 2026-11-17, option (b)): each sending part holds a reservation `max(128, 6*peak)` while its queue is non-empty, 0 once empty (`SendStream::held_spec`, exec `peak` with `peak == buf.peak()` in `wf`); val 9 of `Streams::wf`'s sum (`tx_held`) is the reservation, bounded by `MAX_SEND_BUFFER`; `SendStream::lemma_held` proves the queue's `requested()` (both buffers while migrating) within it, and `Streams::lemma_wf` exports `tx_capacity() <= tx_held() <= MAX_SEND_BUFFER`. `send_room(id)` is `B/6 - len` of the part's share B (0 below 128). Pinned against the allocator by `held_capacity_within_cap` and `room_refills_as_acks_arrive` (stream_bounds.rs). RCA: docs/rca/2026-11-13-byte-buffers.md (mem-9b2-send-cap section). The exact count of fix round 0 was replaced (mem-9b2-send-room).

source: 9b2 Task 8 fix round 0 (2026-11-17); .superpowers/sdd/2026-11-13-phase-9b2-byte-queue/task-8-report.md; owner decision 2026-11-17; fix round 1
text: Send room under the exact capacity count (mem-9b2-send-cap): a write into an empty queue takes at most `MAX_SEND_BUFFER/3` = 349,525 bytes (one buffer of 3x), appends then fill that buffer's first half (174,762 more: a 524,287-byte burst per connection), and from there a 1-byte push would start a migration that keeps both buffers (`ca + 64 > MAX_SEND_BUFFER`, D4 case 3 without the swap), so no sound exact count accepts it: while 3 or more bytes stay unacknowledged every stream of the connection has room 0, and the room returns only when that queue empties (stop-and-wait per 512 KiB on a bulk download; a peer that withholds the last ACK holds it, on its own connection). Pinned by `room_stops_until_queue_empties` (stream_bounds.rs). Option (b) (the reservation `max(128, 6*peak)` per part, peak reset when the queue empties) gives a continuous window of `B/6 - len`, at least `MAX_SEND_BUFFER/6` = 174,762 bytes per connection, refilled as ACKs arrive, and a smaller first write (174,762). Switching is local to send_stream.rs (`held_spec`, `held_after`, `room_spec` over an exec peak, `lemma_room` re-proved); Streams, conn and the tests' structure stay. A third option, the largest d that fits (not a prefix), frees writes of at least about len/2 bytes but refuses some short ones and needs a second closed form. Owner decision. Closed (owner decision 2026-11-17): option (b) shipped. Throughput: under (b) the steady state is about 171 KiB per RTT (the window B/6 refills byte for byte as ACKs arrive, `room_refills_as_acks_arrive`); the exact count gave about 512 KiB per drain + RTT cycle (a 524,287-byte burst, then nothing until the queue empties). Effect on other streams: while one stream's queue is non-empty with peak P, every other stream's room is about (MAX_SEND_BUFFER - 6P)/6, and the reservation stays 6P until that queue next empties (a continuously fed stream may never empty); a stream that peaked at 174,762 takes the whole connection's room. The h3 FIFO (h3_server.rs:4-6, `send_response` refused as Busy while anything waits) already serializes responses, so h3 sees little difference; callers of the quic API and h3's own queued writes wait behind such a stream.
